summary: Casino slot-machine reel symbol (80-byte Ui_Object with vtable 0x007719F8) constructed by the roulette/jackpot windows; the reel animator addresses it through the symbol list and toggles the playing bit at +0x44 of its bound record.
evidence: Ui_SlotSymbol_Ctor (0x0045D584) = Ui_Object_CtorBase, vtable 0x007719F8 at +0 and word +0x4C = 0; the class is named by N_062 and its elements are driven by Ui_SlotMachine_ApplySymbolAnim (0x0045D62C).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_SlotSymbol_Ctor stores 0x007719F8 at +0 immediately after Ui_Object_CtorBase; the deleting dtor walks the vtable, so +0 is the vptr.

fields.name: unknown_4C
fields.evidence: Ctor only writes puVar2[0x13] = 0 (= +0x4C); the sibling Ui_SlotMachine_PartCtor clears +0x4C and +0x50 as well, but no recovered method reads this word, so its purpose is not recoverable.

summary: Stamp-book page object (vtable 0x0076837C) that owns three 0x50-byte stamp-slot animation-reference lists at +0x134; created lazily by Ui_StampBookWindow_Ctor to show the stamps collected on one page.
evidence: Ui_StampBookPage_Ctor stores 0x0076837C at +0 and calls std_ConstructArray(self+0x134, 0x003E0454 Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor, 0x50, 3); 0x134 + 3*0x50 = 0x224, so the batch size 0x138 is only a lower bound (real layout >= 548 bytes).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_StampBookPage_Ctor writes 0x0076837C at +0 (batch constant DAT_003a982c) before the slot array is constructed; the object is only reached through that vtable.

fields.name: stampSlotAnimRefs
fields.evidence: std_ConstructArray(puVar1+0x4d, Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor 0x003E0454, 0x50, 3) constructs a three-element array of 0x50-byte anim-ref lists starting at +0x134 (i.e. 0x134..0x224); the N_088 doc calls them the three stamp-slot records. Recorded width is 4.

summary: One of the two 0x16C-byte child objects built by maybe_Ui_TwoChildObject_Ctor (vtables 0x0076ABD0 / 0x0076AC20); its deleting destructor releases the embedded layout reference at +0x11C and frees the child. 'SubWindow2' was only a copy index.
evidence: maybe_Ui_TwoChildObject_ChildA/B_DeletingDtor (0x003E07EC / 0x003E087C) both do '*self = vtable; Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x11C); func_001D8C2C(ref-0x11C); free'. R3_013 allocates them as two 0x16C-byte children (larger than the 0x120 strong-field size).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Both deleting dtors begin with '*self = vtable' (0x0076ABD0 for child A, 0x0076AC20 for child B); only the destructors install it, the ctor in another class does.

fields.name: layoutRef
fields.evidence: Dtors call Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x11C) and then 'func_001D8C2C(returned - 0x11C)', i.e. the release routine returns the enclosing object; Ui_LayoutRef_Release detaches the pane and drops the owner reference. Recorded width is 4 (embedded head).

summary: Tab state holder of a tabbed window: a byte with the currently applied tab index and a byte with the requested one; Ui_Tab_PlayChangeSe plays SE 0x35/0x36 and resets the matching child-object animation when they differ.
evidence: Ui_Tab_PlayChangeSe (0x003A9960) compares self->f_C with self->f_D, tests f_D for 1 (SE 0x36, reset sub-object 1) and 2 (SE 0x35, reset sub-object 2), then latches f_C = f_D; the two sub-object pointers are at +4 and +8.

fields.name: currentState
fields.evidence: Latched at the end of Ui_Tab_PlayChangeSe ('self->f_c = self->f_d'); it is the tab state that is already applied to the sub-objects, so the branch only runs on a real change.

fields.name: requestedState
fields.evidence: Read five times in Ui_Tab_PlayChangeSe: compared with f_C, tested '== 1' and '== 2' to pick SE 0x36/0x35 and which sub-object animation to reset; it is the requested/target tab state.

summary: Small multi-part text build state used by Ui_TextBuild_Start: a counter that runs up to 50 frames and a flag meaning that some text part still has to be laid out; embedded in the larger TextBuilder.
evidence: Ui_TextBuild_Start (0x00311898) is the first/step call of the multi-part layout: it lays out parts 0..2 into the record, plays SE 0xE70 when the counter reaches 3 and reports completion only when the counter reaches 0x32 (50).

fields.name: frameCounter
fields.evidence: Incremented once per call while layout is pending ('iVar2 = self->f_10 + 1; self->f_10 = iVar2'), SE 0xE70 plays when it becomes 3, and the function returns 0 while it is below 0x32 (50).

fields.name: isLayoutActive
fields.evidence: Assigned from the part-0/count-result of maybe_Text_LayoutEmitStyleRuns and OR-ed with the results for parts 1 and 2; the frame counter only advances while it is non-zero, so it means 'some part still needs layout'. Stored as a word, read as a byte flag.

summary: Per-layer text binding used by message windows and pagers: holds the high (table/layer) half of the packed text id and a pointer to the bound text element; Ui_TextLayer_SetText forwards id + colour to that element.
evidence: Ui_TextLayer_SetText (0x001A629C, 80 callers) only acts when f_34 is set and then calls Ui_Element_SetColor; Ui_TextLayer_SetColorByRatio and Ui_TextLayer_UpdateEnabledItems both build their text id as 'lowPart | self->f_28 << 0x10'.

fields.name: textLayerId
fields.evidence: Ui_TextLayer_SetColorByRatio passes 'id | self->f_28 << 0x10' and Ui_TextLayer_UpdateEnabledItems 'pane | self->f_28 << 0x10' to the text setter; the same u16-at-+0x28 layer key appears in Ui_TextBlink / Ui_DirectionIndicator (S_136/S_137).

fields.name: textElement
fields.evidence: Ui_TextLayer_SetText: 'if (self->f_34 != 0) Ui_Element_SetColor(self->f_34, textId, colour)'; the layer does nothing until a text element is bound here, and the pointer is also reached by Ui_TextElement_SetString callers.

summary: Text-pager state of a multi-page message window: embeds a Ui_TextList page-number state at +0x353C and a polymorphic indicator widget at +0x3574 that is told state 6 or 7 depending on whether a page number exists.
evidence: The update at 0x0030800C calls Ui_TextList_UpdateMeasureState (0x001B827C) on self+0x353C, reads the list's state byte (+0) and page-number flag (+0x2C, i.e. self+0x3568), then dispatches vtable slots +0x14/+0x10 of the object at self+0x3574 with 6/7.

fields.name: textList
fields.evidence: 0x0030800C calls Ui_TextList_UpdateMeasureState on self+0x353C; that function (asm 0x001B827C) reads a state byte at +0, builds a <=6-character page number into the wchar buffer at +0x1C and sets the flag at +0x2C, matching Ui_TextList_CtorSmall's compact list. Width recorded as 4 (embedded head).

fields.name: maybe_pageIndicator
fields.evidence: At self+0x3574 the pager loads a vtable word and calls slot +0x14 with 6 (page number present) or 7, then slot +0x10 - a polymorphic child object embedded at the tail. It is probably the page indicator, but its class is not proven, so the word is left as an opaque placeholder.

summary: Three-line message-window variant (vtable 0x0077B500) whose Init binds the null_txt_l1..l3 templates using the text-id base at +0x28 and then calls vtable slots +0x38/+0x48 to lay them out.
evidence: Ui_ThreeLineTextWindow2_Init (0x004E6E14) calls drN, then three times '(**(code**)(*self+0x38))(self, "null_txt_lN", self->f_28<<16 | n, ...)' and finally '(**(code**)(*self+0x48))(self, self->f_28<<16)'. The disassembly reads ldrh [r4,#0x28] and vtable slots only.

fields.name: maybe_vtableSlot38
fields.evidence: No direct self+0xE0 access: the quoted line is '(**(code **)(*self + 0x38))', a vtable slot at byte +0x38, and struct_db multiplied the slot index by 4 (0x38*4 = 0xE0). It is a scaling artefact, not a field (the real fields are vtable +0 and u16 +0x28).

fields.name: maybe_vtableSlot48
fields.evidence: Same artefact: '(**(code **)(*self + 0x48))(self, ...)' is vtable slot +0x48 and 0x48*4 = 0x120; the asm at 0x004E6E14..0x004E6EF0 reads only +0x28 and vtable slots, so no +0x120 field exists.

summary: In-place-constructed part of the countdown/timer display (vtable 0x00765420) that owns one embedded Ui_AnimRefList at +0x4C; Ui_TimerDisplay_Ctor instantiates it twice inside the display object.
evidence: Ui_TimerDisplayPart_Ctor (0x00368118) = Ui_Object_CtorBase + vtable 0x00765420 at +0 + Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor(self+0x4C), returning base-0x4C; the display ctor calls it on two embedded parts, so the 0x50 strong-field size is only a lower bound (0x4C+0x50 = 0x9C = 156).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_TimerDisplayPart_Ctor writes 0x00765420 at +0; vtable 0x00765420 slot 8 is 0x003680DC (the part's own layout init) and slots 0/1 are its ctor helpers.

fields.name: animRefList
fields.evidence: Disassembly at 0x00368118: 'str vtable,[r0],#0x4c; bl 0x003E0454' - Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor is called in place at +0x4C, so the part embeds a full 0x50-byte animation-reference list and is at least 0x9C bytes. Recorded width is 4 (list head).

summary: Tutorial popup pane (Ui_Effect-derived) that shows one tutorial entry: it binds two label panes keyed by the text-layer id at +0x28 and creates/attaches the 'ui_tutorial_%s.bch' picture through the effect handle at +0x4C.
evidence: Ui_TutorialPane_ShowEntry (0x002D5BBC) looks the id up with 0x0063E3C8, binds panes via func_001A6680(self, self->f_28<<16 | 0/1), formats 'ui_tutorial_%s.bch', creates the effect at &self->f_4c and assigns the handle pair.

fields.name: textLayerId
fields.evidence: ShowEntry calls func_001A6680(self, self->f_28 << 0x10) and ... | 1 for its two label rows; the same u16-at-+0x28 high-half packing of a text-layer key is used by Ui_TextBlink/Ui_DirectionIndicator (S_136/S_137).

fields.name: effectHandle
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_Effect_Create(&self->f_4c, path) creates the tutorial picture there, then Ui_HandlePair_Assign(&self->f_4c) stores it and the code clears bit 0 of the effect flag word; the handle pair starts at +0x4C (recorded width 4).

summary: Tiny scene object (vtable 0x0077635C) holding one float at +0x48; the constructor seeds the -1000.0f 'unset' sentinel and vtable slot 6 publishes the float to (work+8)->f_50->f_F8. Later R3_024 analysis suggests a Field scene object rather than a UI holder.
evidence: maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt77635C (0x004AF5B0) stores 0x0077635C at +0 and 0xC47A0000 (-1000.0f) at puVar2[0x12]=+0x48; maybe_Ui_PublishValueToManager (0x004AF584, vtable slot 6) copies self->f_48 to (work+8)->f_50->f_F8. The 'Ui_ValueHolder' class name is the M1 guess kept as required.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: The ctor stores 0x0077635C at +0; the batch vtable 0x00776360 is the same rodata table seen 4 bytes later. The deleting dtor restores the vptr and calls Ui_Object_DtorBody.

fields.name: value
fields.evidence: Ctor writes the 'no value yet' sentinel -1000.0f (0xC47A0000) at +0x48; slot 6 (maybe_Ui_PublishValueToManager) copies it as a 32-bit float into the manager field (work+8)->f_50 +0xF8 every update, so it is the value this holder publishes (destination meaning still unknown).

summary: Widget host that pushes/pops UI child widgets on a 4-entry stack referenced from +8; PushAt/PushPositionedChild store (child, x, y) triples, bump the depth and notify the new top widget through its virtual callback.
evidence: Ui_WidgetStack_PushAt (0x006D43B8) and PushPositionedChild (0x006D40F8) both read *(self+8) as the stack, test its depth at +0x3C against 4 and write child/x/y at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14+; the InvokeTop variants check the same depth and call vtable +0x14 when it drops below 2.

fields.name: widgetStack
fields.evidence: Every Push/Invoke method dereferences *(self+8) and then indexes the 4-entry stack (depth at +0x3C, entries at +0xC + i*0x18 holding child/x/y); the stack object has no recovered class name in structs.json, so void* is used.

fields.name: maybe_vtableSlot14
fields.evidence: Artefact, not a field: the quoted line '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x14))(param_1)' is vtable slot +0x14 and 0x14*4 = 0x50; the host's vtable is at +0, and no direct +0x50 access exists in any of the eight recovered methods.

summary: UI window resource holder rebuilt by Ui_WindowResource_Reset (reached through GameWork->f_0): dirty byte +4, cached fade animators at +8/+0xC/+0x10 and an aligned allocator at +0x18; Reset allocates a 200-byte curve object and two animators when dirty.
evidence: Ui_WindowResource_Reset (0x002936EC) only touches +4 (dirty byte), +8/+0xC/+0x10 (animator handles, released through vtable +4), +0x18 (Mem_AllocAligned_2 size argument) and re-sets +4=1; Ui_WindowResource_ResetAndInit passes GameWork->f_0 as self and then re-inits the panel node.

fields.name: unknown_00
fields.evidence: The recorded line '*local_2c = DAT_00293984' writes the vtable of the newly allocated 0x37C-byte child (func_001064D4 result), not self; Ui_WindowResource_Reset never reads or writes self+0, so this word is unidentified.

fields.name: unknown_344
fields.evidence: Derived only from 'local_2c = local_2c + 0xd1' (0xd1*4 = 0x344) on that same child pointer; no self+0x344 access exists. The real holder fields observed in Reset are +4/+8/+0xC/+0x10/+0x18.

summary: Window constructor that stores its vtable at +0 and builds a record container at +0x70, whose +0x58 is filled with sixteen 0xE4-byte records; used by the scene-entry/screen-view helpers.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x002B7B58: 'str r1,[r0],#0x70; bl 0x002DB7B4' then std_ConstructArray(returned+0x58, 0x00407740, 0xE4, 0x10). The batch size 0x74 covers only the head; the 16-record array extends the object well past it.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: 'str r1,[r0],#0x70' stores the second constructor argument at +0; callers (Ui_SceneEntry_Add / Gfx_ScreenViews_InitBuffers) pass the window class vtable, the same pattern as every other window ctor.

fields.name: recordContainer
fields.evidence: After the store the ctor advances to self+0x70 and constructs a container there with func_002DB7B4; its +0x58 is then filled by std_ConstructArray with 16 records of 0xE4 bytes (element ctor 0x00407740). No class type for the container is recovered, so void* is a stand-in.

summary: Bag-category helper: Ui_BagCategory_CountItems counts the visible entries of one category in a {owner, entry-array, count} list; the batch also merges maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable, which writes a 7-byte category result buffer, so the recorded +0 write is ambiguous.
evidence: Ui_BagCategory_CountItems (0x006462C4) reads *list (owner), +4 (entry array) and +8 (count) and tests each entry through SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill(*list, entry->u16@8, category); maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable (0x00646BB4) instead writes its 7-byte out buffer ('*out = local_38').

fields.name: maybe_categoryBytes
fields.evidence: Only recorded write is '*param_1 = local_38' in FilterAvailable, which packs the seven surviving category bytes into a 7-byte output (u32+u16+u8); CountItems instead uses +0 as the owner/context. The two functions describe different objects, so +0 is ambiguous.
